report.summary:
S11 is done in worktree <scratch>/wt/p2-s11, branch p2-s11, 7 commits on top of 3c86304. No Go file, template, findings.md, docs/why-small-and-auditable.md or review/phase2_progress.md changed. In review/, only spec §12 changed.

What changed:
- docs/README.md opens with the four areas (signature, node, API/CDN, UI). Each says what it holds, its code, and its docs, followed by a short general list. Every doc states its area in its first lines.
- Two new docs give the areas that had no home one each: docs/signature.md and docs/api.md. The HTTP API moved out of operating-a-network.md into api.md, and the signature passages from the README moved into signature.md.
- Every doc was rewritten against the code at the branch head, covering every row of the §11 table and every S11 note:
  - ML-DSA-65 and the seed; names as the identity; registration at a bank; key and bank changes; the freeze, including the 64-block window; the ⅔ name action.
  - The block hash with its nonce and signing set; proposal evidence, the one-third cap and pending proofs; a node signs only while seated with its key.
  - The checkpoint and the order its checks run in; the genesis file and the node config, which refuses unknown keys; the effective network id, with a new networkName at every new genesis.
  - The record: units of 100, files named by network, from=H, the newest unit with no from, a negative from answered 400, the folder listing and its cost, pruning only when the oldest unit is due, the full scan of the lifelong file, and deleting old record files at a new genesis.
  - The idle chain and what it costs; catch-up asks /hdls/status first; the last commit for a node one precommit short; the maxPaymentAmount line, in both places.
  - The wallet's Requests page, the bank's desk, the payment review, hash names, the new .state fields, "did not land", "wait for the chain to advance", and the copy button that needs a secure context.
  - The S10 open points are stated as current behaviour, with no fix promised.
- findings_20261027.md: each Phase 2 item is marked fixed with its slice, after I checked the fix in the code:
  - E1, E6 and E7 (S2); E9 (S3, S5); E13 (S6); E15 (S4); E16 (S4, S6); E20 (S4, S8); E29 (S5, S9); E38 (S4); E44 (S5).
  - Also E35's freeze (S6, S10), E43's dropped domains (S1), and E12's better fix (S4).
  - The Phase 2 decisions are marked built, and the closing limits say what Phase 2 changed. Phase 3 stays as planned.
- Spec §12: the owner's dated decisions are listed (2026-10-28 cost vs cap; 2026-10-30 freeze window, record named by network, units of 100, four areas, S12). Q3, Q4 and Q24 are annotated, the column is now "Builder default", and the S10 points still waiting for the owner are listed.
- README.md: its stale sections are rewritten. The Layout section is byte-identical, since S12 replaces it. The images are captioned as pages from before Phase 2.

Checks I ran in scratch copies:
- All binaries build, and `go test -short ./...` passes.
- keygen's output matches the docs.
- The genesis and node-config examples in operating-a-network.md, extracted from the doc with only keys and addresses substituted, ran as a 4-bank network: it committed block 1 and idled.
- An unknown config key is refused.
- The record routes, resolve and governance answer as documented.
- A wallet payment woke the chain and the chain idled again afterwards; a wallet freeze landed.
- The demo runs. The manual's registration flow (draft, sign as new key, bank signs, submit) worked end to end and registered the name after about 125 s, matching the 120-block lead.
- The founder's own freeze is refused with the "no name seated" reason (R9).
- Every link and anchor in the edited docs resolves.

The docs grew from about 22,700 words to about 25,100 (+10%).

So ui/main.go vote shows "certificate submitted — it enacts in the next block" even for a certificate the node refused. The wallet's Submit checks Valid first, so this happens only when the state moved in between.

codeNotes.note: These go through the event loop (Node.Snapshot or GovernanceView), and Snapshot copies the account list. handleResolve reads the committed view off the loop. problems.problem: The sign log section says: "Once the snapshot of height h is on disk, the node writes an empty log for h + 1 (`Node.commit`). So an idle node keeps no block, no payment and no nonce." This is false for the node as a whole. Only the sign log is emptied. (1) The snapshot keeps the last block's header, and the header includes its nonce. (2) In memory, the node keeps the whole last decided block until the next commit, payments included.
problems.evidence: node/persist.go saveSnapshot writes savedSnapshot{Checkpoint: node.snapshot().checkpoint()}. node/messages.go Checkpoint.LastBlock is a ledger.BlockHeader, and ledger/hash.go BlockHeader has a Nonce field. I ran a 1-validator network in a scratch copy. After block 1 it idled. data/snapshot.json held Checkpoint.LastBlock.Nonce, and GET /hdls/checkpoint served the same nonce. docs/consensus.md also lists the nonce in the checkpoint header. In node/node.go, Node.commit sets node.lastProposal = node.heightProposals[decision.Round]. That is a ProposalMessage carrying the whole ledger.Block, and it stays in memory until the next commit, for sendLastCommit. Also, Node.commit writes the empty log only when node.signLog.Height == block.Height, that is, when the node signed at h. Spec §3.6 says "an idle chain does not keep the last block". The code keeps that block in memory, so no doc can promise this without a code change.
problems.fix: Limit the sentence to the sign log: "So while the chain idles, the sign log holds no block, no payment and no nonce." Optionally add: "The snapshot keeps the last block's header, its nonce included, as the checkpoint serves it. The node keeps the last decided proposal, block included, in memory until the next commit, to re-send the last commit." Write "a node whose log holds h writes an empty log for h + 1". Tell the owner that spec §3.6's "does not keep the last block" is true only of the disk.

problems.problem: No doc says how a keygen pair gets into a wallet, or how a wallet's key gets into the genesis or the node config. Several procedures depend on it. The bank's desk and the bank's freeze button need "the bank operator's wallet, which holds the bank's one key". Genesis accounts get their keys from keygen, but their holders use wallets. The leaked-key runbook says in step 2 "Make a new key with `keygen`" and in step 3 "The new key's wallet signs the proof first", but no wallet holds that key. ui/README.md even says "a key import or export flow are future work". So an operator cannot complete the procedure as written.
problems.evidence: cmd/demo/main.go writeWallet gives the founder's wallet its key by writing {"publicKey","privateKey"}. ui/keyfile.go loadOrCreateKey accepts that plaintext form and offers to seal it. In a scratch copy I wrote keygen's two lines as {"publicKey":"…","privateKey":"…"} into w/wallet.json. `wallet -wallet w/wallet.json` loaded it and logged the keygen key's prefix ("key Fzd6p8aaqRzq…"). grep finds no doc that describes this. ui/README.md, ui/USER_MANUAL.md and docs/operating-a-network.md only say that the wallet creates its own key on first run.
problems.fix: Add a short paragraph to operating-a-network.md "Generate keys" and link it from "A bank whose key leaked" step 3. It says: a wallet can hold a keygen pair. Before the wallet's first start, write its key file as {"publicKey": "<publicKey>", "privateKey": "<privateKey>"}. The wallet then asks for a passphrase and seals the key. A bank operator's wallet holds the bank's pair this way, and so does a genesis account's wallet. In ui/README.md "Its files", say the same, and reword "a key import or export flow are future work".

problems.problem: "A name that doesn't say who you are" says the hash name is "`k-` followed by 26 letters and digits made from your key". In fact 24 characters follow `k-`, and the whole name is 26 characters long. This is at the edge of the signature area: the name is derived from the key.
problems.evidence: ui/requests.go hashName returns "k-" + lowercase base32 of the first 15 bytes of SHA-256, and 15 bytes give 24 base32 characters (checked: len(b32encode(bytes(15))) == 24). Spec §7.7 says "26 characters" for the whole name, and ui/README.md agrees.
problems.fix: "`k-` followed by 24 letters and digits made from your key (26 characters in all)".

problems.problem: "An observer, a node whose name is not seated, never signs." docs/operating-a-network.md, leaked-key step 4, also says the node "signs nothing" until it restarts with the new key. Both are wrong. Every node signs a receipt for each payment it newly pools, with its configured key. So a re-keyed bank's node keeps signing receipts with the old, leaked key until it restarts. Separately, "Generate keys" says only that validators and genesis accounts need a key pair. An observer also needs one: the config refuses an empty key.
problems.evidence: node/httptransport.go handlePay calls ledger.SignReceipt(server.node.config.Signer, server.node.config.Name, payment) whether or not the node is seated. Node.seatedSigner controls only the driver's votes and proposals. cmd/server/config.go load refuses a publicKey that is not 1952 bytes long, an empty one included.
problems.fix: Write "signs no vote or proposal (it still signs payment receipts with its configured key)" in consensus.md and in operating step 4. In "Generate keys", say that every node needs a key pair, an observer too.

problems.problem: signature.md, README.md (Signatures) and security.md say there is no "sign these raw bytes" call. The package does export one. `MLDSA65.ParsePrivateKey` returns a `signing.PrivateKey`, and its exported `Sign(message []byte)` signs any bytes. Only `Signer.Sign` calls it in production code. The claim holds for the Signer API, not for the package.
problems.evidence: In signing/scheme.go, the PrivateKey interface has Sign(message []byte) ([]byte, error). signing/mldsa65.go mldsa65Key.Sign calls SignDeterministic(message, nil). A grep finds production calls only in signing/signer.go Signer.Sign (ui/keyfile.go only derives the public key).
problems.fix: "`Signer`, the only signing API the node and the wallet use, has no raw-bytes call. The scheme's `PrivateKey.Sign` signs whatever it is given, and only `Signer.Sign` calls it, with a domain-tagged preimage."

problems.problem: "A double-sign is two signatures by a name's current key for different blocks in one slot" appears in signature.md, and README.md says "for different blocks" too. The code counts two different block hashes, so a nil vote (all zeros) against a vote for a block also freezes the name. Also, "Any node that sees both keeps them as a proof" is too broad. A node keeps a proof only from the three sources consensus.md lists. For example, a conflicting prevote that arrives after the node has left that height is dropped.
problems.evidence: consensus/evidence.go VoteEvidence.Valid requires only First.BlockHash != Second.BlockHash. node/node.go recordLateDoubleSign returns at once unless the vote is a precommit for lastCommit's height and round. docs/consensus.md correctly says "with different block hashes" and names the three sources.
problems.fix: Write "for different block hashes (a nil vote counts as one)", and "a node that sees both, in the places consensus.md lists, keeps them as a proof".

problems.problem: "What a double-sign costs" gives only part of the cost. It says the name leaves the set, keeps its balance and is unfrozen only with a new key. It leaves out three costs a bank operator needs to know. The frozen name neither pays nor is paid. Freezing a bank clears every pending change it co-signed, so its customers must file again and lose the fee. The node signs no vote until its config holds the new key.
problems.evidence: ledger/name_request.go freezeNames clears the frozen name's own pending change and every PendingKey whose Bank is frozen or PendingBank that is frozen. ledger/block.go refuses payments from or to a frozen name. Node.seatedSigner returns nil when the name is seated under another key. docs/architecture.md ("A freeze") and operating-a-network.md ("A bank whose key leaked") state these facts. signature.md does not link to them.
problems.fix: Add one or two sentences: "A frozen name neither pays nor is paid. Freezing a bank clears every pending change it co-signed. After the ⅔ re-key, the node signs again only once its config holds the new pair (see operating-a-network.md#a-bank-whose-key-leaked)."

problems.problem: "The freeze and its limits" says "nodes that lag and wallets that pinned it then need a new seed or a new list". Everywhere else in the docs, "seed" means the 32-byte private key. A reader could take this as "make a new key". The spec (§5.8, "a re-seed") means a new trust anchor: a snapshot from a trusted node.
problems.evidence: signature.md and the ui docs use "seed" only for the private key. operating-a-network.md#rejoining-after-a-restart gives the actual remedy: copy a trusted node's snapshot.
problems.fix: "nodes that lag then need a snapshot from a node you trust (see operating-a-network.md#rejoining-after-a-restart), and wallets that pinned it need a new list."

problems.problem: The Status section says "Phase 3, the split into a signer, an engine and an edge proxy", which is three parts. The other docs say four. docs/README.md says the docs follow "the four parts Phase 3 splits the system into, one container each". TODO.md lists four containers (signer, engine, fetcher, wallet). The owner said on 2026-10-30: "4 docker containers: signature, node, api/cdn and ui".
problems.evidence: README.md, Status, paragraph after the list. docs/README.md, first paragraph. TODO.md, Phase 3 item. Spec §11, "Four areas".
problems.fix: "Phase 3, the split into four containers, one per docs area (a signer, an engine, an edge proxy and the wallet), is planned, not built".

problems.problem: The Fan-out bullet says "With `maxPeers` 0 every node gossips to every peer it knows". Once every current validator has an address, which is true in the doc's own genesis example, a validator's peers become the other validators' addresses, and its configured `peers` are no longer used. With maxPeers above 0, the topology applies only once every validator has an address. And a non-validator node (an observer, such as a wallet's reference node) then gets no proposals, votes or payments pushed to it. It follows the chain only by checkpoint catch-up.

In cmd/server/config.go, `load` uses the topology only when `haveAll` is true. Node.commit calls `resolvePeersFromState` after every block.
problems.fix: Rewrite the bullet: "A node gossips to its configured `peers` until every current validator has an address. Then a validator gossips to the other validators: to all of them with `maxPeers` 0, or to its topology neighbours (`node.Neighbors`) with `maxPeers` above 0.
